evidence_quotes.agenda: 'What are your biggest concerns on your move? What are the most important things you want answers on this call today?' — asked as the very first substantive question, before any logistics probing.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised a real concern (time-constrained, needs the Sleep Number bed disconnected/reconnected, wants help packing) and the rep clarified what packing service covers, but didn't dig further into her time pressure or other worries before moving to the estimate.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: Only the generic actual-hours-billed framing landed; no rate-commit line, no explicit pay-less-if-faster line, no self-prep tip, no 'does that feel fair' check.

top_strength: Opened with the agenda question first thing, exactly as scripted — a genuinely strong start that most other calls in this batch missed.
coaching_note: When the customer pushed back on the 7-hour estimate ('that's too much'), the rep only revised the number reactively rather than reframing it proactively with the estimate-is-a-window language up front — leading directly into her price objection and the call ending without a close attempt.
